# CREST Registered Tester (CRT) Study Materials

A personal collection of preparation materials for the [CREST Registered Tester (CRT)](https://www.crest-approved.org/skills-certifications-careers/crt/) examination, covering the syllabus published by CREST. Includes a study guide, a comprehensive study book, a quick-reference cheat sheet, and a CRESTDrive reference pack of the kind candidates can pre-load before the exam.

## ⚠️ Important Caveat

**These materials were generated by [Claude](https://claude.ai), an AI assistant by Anthropic.** While effort has been made to verify content against the official CREST CRT syllabus and FAQ, **the materials may contain errors, omissions, or outdated information**.

In particular:

- **Always verify exam structure, duration, format, and pass criteria against the current official CREST documentation** ([Notes for Candidates](https://www.crest-approved.org/skills-certifications-careers/crt-faqs/) and the current syllabus PDF) before relying on any procedural detail.
- Technical commands, payloads, and exploit references should be tested in a safe lab environment — do not assume any command works exactly as shown without verifying it.
- The lists of default credentials, exploit CVEs, and tool flags reflect a snapshot in time; tools and vendor defaults change.
- Some content (notably the "condensed" versions of GTFOBins and PayloadsAllTheThings) is by definition incomplete — refer to the original source repositories for full coverage.

**Use these materials as a starting point and study aid, not as a substitute for hands-on practice and authoritative documentation.** If you find errors, please open an issue or pull request.

These materials are shared in the hope they are useful to others preparing for the CRT, but with no warranty of accuracy or fitness for purpose.

---

## Repository Contents

The repository contains four sets of materials. All are provided in both Markdown source and PDF format. The Markdown is the primary source of truth; the PDFs are generated from it for portable reading.

### 1. Study Guide — `CRT_Study_Guide.md` / `CRT_Study_Guide.pdf`

A concise (~8-page) guide to the exam itself: format, structure, timing, the published syllabus mapped to skill areas (Appendices A through H), and a 4-week study plan. Read this first.

### 2. Study Book — `CRT_Study_Book.md` / `CRT_Study_Book.pdf`

A comprehensive (~58,000 words, ~155-page) technical reference covering the entire CRT syllabus across 12 chapters:

| Part | Topic | Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Exam Introduction & Core Technical Skills | Appendix A: nmap fluency, OS fingerprinting, methodology |
| 2 | DNS & Reconnaissance | Appendix B: zone transfers, subdomain discovery, OSINT |
| 3 | Networks | Appendix C: IPv4/TCP/UDP fundamentals, VLANs, traffic analysis, **routing manipulation/pivoting** (SSH tunnels, chisel, ligolo-ng, sshuttle) |
| 4 | Network Services | Appendix D: TLS/SSL, Telnet, FTP, Responder/LLMNR/NTLM relay, SMB, LDAP, SNMP, NFS, SMTP, SSH, etc. |
| 5 | Microsoft Windows Security Assessment | Appendices E1-E13: AD enumeration, BloodHound, Kerberoasting, AS-REP roasting, password spraying, Windows hashes, post-exploitation, mimikatz, lateral movement, privesc, **Desktop Lockdown breakouts** |
| 6 | Linux/UNIX Security Assessment | Appendix F: passwords, SUID/SGID/capabilities, GTFOBins, sudo, cron, NFS no_root_squash, kernel exploits (PwnKit, Dirty Pipe), Docker/LXD privesc, BSD/Solaris specifics |
| 7 | Web Technologies (Part 1) | Appendix G1-G14: web servers, CMSs, frameworks, HTTP/HTTPS, cookies, sessions, JWT, **SQL injection**, authentication & authorisation, XSS, CSRF |
| 8 | Web Technologies (Part 2) | Appendix G15-G23: mail injection, OS command injection, file uploads, parameter manipulation, business logic, web crypto, directory traversal, SSTI, SSRF |
| 9 | Databases | Appendix H: SQL fundamentals, MSSQL (xp_cmdshell, linked servers), MySQL (FILE privilege, UDF), Oracle (TNS, ODAT), PostgreSQL (COPY FROM PROGRAM), NoSQL |
| 10 | HackTheBox / TryHackMe Walkthroughs | Specific machine recommendations mapped to each syllabus area, plus worked walkthroughs of HTB Forest (AD) and HTB Bashed (Linux web → root) |
| 11 | Exam Strategy & Preparation | Time allocation for the 2.5-hour exam, decision heuristics, mock exam guidance, 8-week study plan, common mistakes |
| 12 | Appendices & Cheat Sheets | Common ports, hashcat modes, default credentials, reverse shells, SQL/XSS payloads, AD attack chain, Linux/Windows privesc checklists |

### 3. Cheat Sheet — `CRT_Cheat_Sheet.md` / `CRT_Cheat_Sheet.pdf`

A dense (~9-page) command reference suitable for fast in-exam lookup. Covers the most-reached-for commands across nmap, ffuf, sqlmap, hashcat, impacket, Active Directory attack tooling, reverse shells, and privilege escalation.

### 4. CRESTDrive Reference Pack — `CRESTDrive_Reference_Pack.zip` / `CRESTDrive_Reference_Pack.pdf` / `CRESTDrive_Reference_Pack.md`

Twelve standalone reference files designed for upload to [CRESTDrive](https://www.crest-approved.org/skills-certifications-careers/crt-faqs/) — the candidate-uploaded file area available during the CRT exam. Provided in three formats:

- **`.zip`** — twelve individual `.md` files for granular per-topic upload
- **`.pdf`** — single 118-page combined reference (~1 MB)
- **`.md`** — single combined Markdown source

The 12 reference files inside the zip are:

| # | File | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| 01 | `01_command_reference.md` | Personal command reference: every nmap, ffuf, sqlmap, hydra, hashcat, john, NetExec/CrackMapExec, impacket, smbclient/smbmap, ldapsearch, evil-winrm, Burp, msfvenom command syntax used routinely |
| 02 | `02_gtfobins_condensed.md` | The most-needed entries from [GTFOBins](https://gtfobins.github.io) — SUID, sudo, capability, and limited-binary exploitation patterns |
| 03 | `03_payloads_condensed.md` | A selection from [PayloadsAllTheThings](https://github.com/swisskyrepo/PayloadsAllTheThings) covering SQL injection, XSS, SSTI, OS command injection, path traversal, SSRF, XXE, file upload bypasses, JWT attacks, and AD-specific attacks |
| 04 | `04_reverse_shells.md` | Comprehensive reverse shell catalogue: bash, sh, netcat, Python, PHP, Perl, Ruby, Node, Java, PowerShell, Windows-specific, and shell stabilisation techniques (including socat full-PTY upgrade) |
| 05 | `05_common_ports.md` | Service-to-port and port-to-service lookup tables, including DC port profile recognition |
| 06 | `06_hash_reference.md` | Hash format identification by appearance, hashcat / john mode lookup, hash-to-source mapping (secretsdump, GetUserSPNs, Responder, /etc/shadow), and crack-time guidance |
| 07 | `07_default_credentials.md` | Default credentials for routers, switches, firewalls, hypervisors, databases, web applications, monitoring tools, and the universal "first 20 to try" |
| 08 | `08_ad_methodology.md` | Stepwise Active Directory attack methodology: domain controller identification → null session enumeration → AS-REP roasting → password spraying → Kerberoasting → BloodHound analysis → ACL abuse → DCSync → Domain Admin |
| 09 | `09_web_methodology.md` | Phase-by-phase web application testing checklist: reconnaissance, authentication, authorisation, input validation, session management, business logic, configuration |
| 10 | `10_exploits_cves.md` | Well-known exploits with CVE numbers and Metasploit module names, organised by service category (SMB, Web, Database, AD, Linux kernel, Windows) |
| 11 | `11_linux_privesc.md` | Linux privilege escalation playbook: situational awareness → sudo / SUID / capabilities / cron / writable files → group-based (docker, lxd, disk) → stored credentials → NFS → kernel exploits |
| 12 | `12_windows_privesc.md` | Windows privilege escalation playbook: `whoami /priv` → SeImpersonate / Potato family → service misconfigurations → AlwaysInstallElevated → stored credentials → UAC bypass → ACL abuse → kernel exploits |

### Note on Items 2 and 3 in the CRESTDrive Pack

The condensed versions of **GTFOBins** and **PayloadsAllTheThings** included here are curated subsets, not full mirrors. The original repositories are large (PayloadsAllTheThings is approximately 600 MB) and are best obtained directly:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/GTFOBins/GTFOBins.github.io.git
git clone https://github.com/swisskyrepo/PayloadsAllTheThings.git
```

Consider zipping these repositories and uploading them alongside the CRESTDrive Reference Pack for full coverage during the exam.

## Suggested Reading Order

For someone starting from scratch:

1. **`CRT_Study_Guide.pdf`** — orient yourself to the exam in 8 pages
2. **`CRT_Study_Book.pdf`** — work through chapters 1-9 alongside lab practice (HackTheBox, TryHackMe, PortSwigger Web Security Academy)
3. **Chapter 10** of the study book — pick HTB / THM machines to practise
4. **Chapter 11** — exam strategy, 8 weeks before the exam
5. **`CRT_Cheat_Sheet.pdf`** and **`CRESTDrive_Reference_Pack.zip`** — upload to CRESTDrive shortly before the exam

For an experienced tester refreshing for the exam:

1. **Skim** `CRT_Study_Guide.pdf` to confirm syllabus coverage
2. **Targeted reading** of weak areas from `CRT_Study_Book.pdf`
3. **Practise** a handful of HTB / THM boxes from chapter 10
4. **Pre-load** `CRT_Cheat_Sheet.pdf` and `CRESTDrive_Reference_Pack.zip` into CRESTDrive

## How These Materials Were Built

The Markdown sources were generated through multiple iterations of structured prompting with [Claude](https://claude.ai), cross-referenced against:

- The official [CREST CRT syllabus](https://www.crest-approved.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/CREST-CRT-Syllabus-V2.0.pdf) v2.0
- The official [CREST CRT FAQ](https://www.crest-approved.org/skills-certifications-careers/crt-faqs/)

The PDFs were generated from the Markdown sources using `pandoc` and `wkhtmltopdf` with custom CSS for a clean reference-text layout.

If you want to regenerate the PDFs after editing the Markdown:

```bash
# Combined CRESTDrive PDF
pandoc CRESTDrive_Reference_Pack.md -o CRESTDrive_Reference_Pack.html \
    --standalone --css=style.css \
    --from markdown-yaml_metadata_block-tex_math_dollars-tex_math_single_backslash

wkhtmltopdf --enable-local-file-access \
    --margin-top 18mm --margin-bottom 18mm \
    --margin-left 16mm --margin-right 16mm \
    --user-style-sheet style.css \
    CRESTDrive_Reference_Pack.html CRESTDrive_Reference_Pack.pdf
```

The same pattern applies to the Study Book and Study Guide.

## Contributing

Corrections and additions are welcome. If you spot something wrong, please:

- Open an issue describing the error and citing the authoritative source
- Or submit a pull request with the fix

Particularly valuable corrections:

- Errors in command syntax that would fail in a real exam environment
- Outdated CVE references or Metasploit module names
- Default credentials that have changed or been deprecated
- Mistakes in the AD attack chain commands
- Anything in chapter 11 (exam strategy) that disagrees with current CREST documentation
